s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic facial swelling with reduced mouth opening and prior similar episodes
salient_findings: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
Reduced mouth opening
Gross right facial asymmetry
Ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders
Elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa
key_facts: 62-year-old man
Two-week history of facial swelling
Two prior similar episodes over eight years
No pain or fever
Known diabetic on regular medication
6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling
Swelling extended from the level of the right lateral canthus to 1 cm below the corner of the mouth
Restricted mouth opening due to the mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas
Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content
Erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla
Maxillary antrum was compressed

shortlist.label: Branchial cleft cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic facial swelling with prior similar episodes and imaging showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas

shortlist.label: Odontogenic cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Restricted mouth opening and imaging showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the buccal space

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders and normal overlying skin

shortlist.label: Chronic sclerosing sialadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of prior similar episodes and imaging showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Soft to firm consistency of the swelling and absence of lymphadenopathy or paresthesia
